question.problem: Given the elliptic paraboloid $z+4=\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}$, find its intercepts with the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the paraboloid, we substitute $y=0$ and $z=0$ into the equation of the paraboloid and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}0+4 & =\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(0-2)^{2}}{4} \\ 4 & =\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{4}{4} \\ 4 & =\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{3}+1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{3} & =3 \\ (x-4)^{2} & =9 \\ x-4 & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the solutions $x=1,7.$

Therefore, the intercepts with the $x$-axis are $(1,0,0)$ and $(7,0,0).$
